implementation_notes: JavaScript's sprawl is unusually easy to create because each service is a directory with a `package.json` and the deployment story looks free, and the cost is deferred: N `package.json` files means N dependency-update pull requests, N audit surfaces and N sets of possibly-diverging lockfiles. Serverless makes it worse, because a function per operation is the default shape of a `serverless.yml` and the per-invocation cost is multiplied by the fan-out. The consolidation is one deployable with a router, which Node makes cheap; the detection is the count of `package.json` files and of deployment manifests.
idiom_name: one npm package or Lambda per function; Express app per entity
pitfalls: N lockfiles means N dependency-update pull requests and N audit surfaces for the same transitive dependency tree.
A `serverless.yml` with one function per operation makes every business operation a fan-out with per-invocation cost.
Package versions drift because each service's lockfile is updated independently, so a shared library upgrade is N breaking changes.
